questions.q:
Statement-I: In an n-type semiconductor, the majority charge carriers are holes.
Statement-II: An n-type semiconductor is produced by doping a pure semiconductor with a pentavalent impurity such as phosphorus.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: A pentavalent atom donates an extra free electron to the crystal, so electrons are the majority carriers in n-type material. Holes are the majority carriers in p-type material, doped with trivalent impurities such as boron.
questions.h: n = negative = electrons; p = positive = holes.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about semiconductor devices:
1. A light-emitting diode emits light when it is forward biased.
2. A photodiode is normally operated in reverse bias.
3. A solar cell needs an external forward bias to generate electricity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: In an LED, electrons and holes recombine under forward bias and release photons. A photodiode in reverse bias gives a current that varies with light, while a solar cell generates its own voltage from light with no external bias.
questions.h: LED: Forward = Fire the light; Photodiode: Reverse = Read the light.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics for the transistor was awarded to Jack Kilby.
2. The transistor was invented at Bell Laboratories in 1947.
3. The first working integrated circuit was demonstrated by Jack Kilby at Texas Instruments.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Bardeen, Brattain and Shockley of Bell Labs received the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics for the transistor. Kilby demonstrated the first integrated circuit in 1958 and received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2000.

questions.q: Moore's Law, often cited in the context of electronics, refers to the observation that
o: the number of transistors on an integrated circuit doubles roughly every two years
the speed of a processor doubles every year at half the cost
the power consumed by a chip halves every year
the size of a data centre doubles every two years
questions.e: Gordon Moore observed in 1965 that the number of components on a chip doubled every year, later revising it to about two years. It drove falling cost per transistor and rising computing power, though physical limits are now slowing it.
questions.h: Moore = more transistors, every two years.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) and related projects:
1. The Programme for Development of Semiconductors and Display Manufacturing Ecosystem was approved in December 2021.
2. Micron Technology's assembly and test facility in India is located at Sanand, Gujarat.
3. The Tata Electronics-PSMC semiconductor fabrication plant is planned at Dholera, Gujarat.
4. The India Semiconductor Mission functions under the Ministry of Heavy Industries.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The first three statements are correct. The ISM is part of the Digital India Corporation under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), not the Ministry of Heavy Industries.
questions.s: PIB, MeitY; Union Cabinet decisions on semiconductors

questions.q:
With reference to the semiconductor industry, consider the following statements:
1. A fabless company designs chips but outsources their manufacturing to a foundry.
2. OSAT firms design the architecture of the chips.
3. A foundry manufactures chips designed by other companies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The chip value chain runs from design (fabless firms) to fabrication (foundries) to assembly and testing. OSAT stands for outsourced semiconductor assembly and test, so these firms package and test chips rather than design them.
questions.h: Fabless designs, Foundry fabricates, OSAT packs.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography is used to make the most advanced chips with very small features.
Statement-II: EUV uses light of a much shorter wavelength (about 13.5 nm) than earlier deep-ultraviolet systems (193 nm).
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The smallest feature that can be printed on a wafer depends on the wavelength of light used, so a shorter wavelength allows finer circuit patterns. This is why EUV machines are central to advanced-node chips.
questions.s: Standard technology references; ASML / IEEE Spectrum

questions.q:
Match List-I (Sensor) with List-II (Quantity it senses):
List-I
A. LiDAR
B. Gyroscope
C. Hall-effect sensor
D. Thermistor
List-II
1. Magnetic field
2. Temperature
3. Angular velocity (rotation)
4. Distance using laser pulses
questions.e: LiDAR times reflected laser pulses to measure distance, a gyroscope senses rotation, a Hall sensor responds to magnetic fields and a thermistor changes resistance with temperature. These sensors are the 'senses' of smartphones, cars and IoT devices.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Physics; standard electronics texts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about RFID and related technologies:
1. FASTag uses radio frequency identification (RFID) technology for toll payment.
2. Near Field Communication (NFC) works over a very short range of a few centimetres.
3. A passive RFID tag contains its own battery to transmit data.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A passive tag has no battery and is powered by the electromagnetic field of the reader, which is why it is cheap enough for toll tags and inventory. NFC is a short-range form of RFID used in contactless payment.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a characteristic of laser light?
o: It consists of many wavelengths with random phases
questions.e: Laser light (Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation) is coherent, nearly single-wavelength and travels as a narrow beam. Ordinary sources such as bulbs produce many wavelengths with random phases.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Physics, Atoms / Wave Optics

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about optical fibres:
1. They transmit light signals by total internal reflection.
2. The cladding has a higher refractive index than the core.
3. Charles Kao shared the 2009 Nobel Prize in Physics for work on fibre optics for communication.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Light stays inside the fibre because the core has a higher refractive index than the cladding, enabling total internal reflection. Reversing the two indices would let light escape.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Physics, Ray Optics; NobelPrize.org

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about superconductivity:
1. A superconductor working at room temperature and ordinary pressure is commercially in use.
2. Superconductors show zero electrical resistance below a critical temperature.
3. The Meissner effect is the expulsion of magnetic field from a superconductor.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Superconducting magnets cooled by liquid helium are used in MRI machines. Practical superconductors still need very low temperatures or high pressure, and claims of room-temperature superconductivity (such as LK-99 in 2023) were not confirmed.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Physics; Nature news on LK-99

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about graphene:
1. It is a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a hexagonal lattice.
2. Geim and Novoselov won the 2010 Nobel Prize in Physics for work on it.
3. It is a poor conductor of electricity.
4. It is an allotrope of silicon.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Graphene is a one-atom-thick sheet of carbon, an allotrope of carbon like graphite and diamond, and it conducts electricity and heat very well. Statements 3 and 4 are therefore wrong.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Quantum dots of different sizes emit light of different colours.
Statement-II: Smaller quantum dots confine electrons more strongly and emit shorter-wavelength (bluer) light.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: In a quantum dot the energy gap depends on its size, so smaller dots emit bluer light and larger dots redder light. The 2023 Nobel Prize in Chemistry went to Bawendi, Brus and Ekimov for the discovery and synthesis of quantum dots.
questions.h: Small dot = Blue; Big dot = Red.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 2014 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded for the invention of efficient blue light-emitting diodes.
2. The UJALA scheme for distributing energy-efficient LED lamps is implemented by Energy Efficiency Services Limited.
3. LED lamps have a shorter operating life than incandescent bulbs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Blue LEDs made white LED lighting possible, as blue light plus phosphor gives white. LEDs last many times longer than incandescent bulbs while using far less power, which is the basis of the UJALA scheme of the Ministry of Power.
questions.h: LED: Forward = Fire the light; Photodiode: Reverse = Read the light.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the microwave oven:
1. Metal utensils are ideal for it because they absorb microwaves efficiently.
2. It uses a device called a magnetron to produce microwaves.
3. Microwaves heat food mainly by making polar molecules such as water rotate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Water molecules are dipoles that try to align with the rapidly oscillating field (about 2.45 GHz), and the friction heats the food. Metal reflects microwaves and can cause sparks, so it is unsuitable.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Radar uses radio waves or microwaves to detect objects.
2. Radar is the preferred technology for detecting submarines deep under water because radio waves penetrate seawater easily.
3. Doppler radar uses the change in frequency of reflected waves to estimate the velocity of a target.
4. Sonar uses microwaves for underwater detection.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Radar and Doppler radar (also used by the IMD for weather) are correct. Radio waves are absorbed quickly by seawater, so sonar uses sound waves for underwater detection.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Physics, Electromagnetic Waves; Class 11 Physics, Waves

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about gallium nitride (GaN):
1. It is a wide band-gap semiconductor.
2. Gallium is one of the rare earth elements.
3. It is used in compact fast chargers and radio-frequency power amplifiers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A wide band gap lets GaN devices handle high voltage, temperature and frequency with less energy loss. Gallium is a metal but not one of the 17 rare earth elements, though like them it is a critical mineral for electronics.
questions.s: MeitY / Ministry of Mines on critical minerals

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The National Policy on Electronics 2019 aims to make India a global hub for Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM).
2. The Production Linked Incentive scheme for large-scale electronics manufacturing was launched in 2020.
3. Both are administered by the Ministry of Heavy Industries.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Electronics policy and schemes such as PLI for mobile phones and components are run by MeitY, not the Ministry of Heavy Industries.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about transformers:
1. A transformer works only with alternating current.
2. An ideal step-up transformer increases the output power.
3. In a step-up transformer, the secondary coil has more turns than the primary.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A transformer works on mutual induction, which needs a changing magnetic flux and therefore AC. A step-up transformer raises voltage but lowers current, so power is conserved (and slightly lost in real transformers).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about semiconductor materials:
1. Silicon is rarer than germanium in the Earth's crust.
2. Germanium was used in the earliest transistors.
3. Gallium arsenide is a compound semiconductor used in LEDs and microwave devices.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Early transistors were germanium, but silicon took over because it is abundant (second most abundant element in the crust, after oxygen) and works better at higher temperatures.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about e-waste in India:
1. The E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 are based on the principle of Extended Producer Responsibility.
2. These rules came into effect on 1 April 2023.
3. Under these rules only government-owned agencies may recycle e-waste.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 2022 rules make producers responsible for collection and recycling through EPR certificates traded on a central portal. Recycling is done by registered recyclers, including private ones, not only by government bodies.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the basic working principle of a solar photovoltaic cell?
o: Generation of a voltage when light falls on a p-n junction
Generation of electricity from a temperature difference between two metals
Generation of voltage when a crystal is mechanically stressed
Deflection of charge carriers by a magnetic field
questions.e: Photons create electron-hole pairs near a p-n junction, and the junction's built-in field separates them, giving a photovoltaic voltage. The other options describe the Seebeck, piezoelectric and Hall effects.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about display technology:
1. A resistive touchscreen works by sensing the change in capacitance caused by a finger.
2. Each pixel of an OLED display emits its own light.
3. A conventional LCD requires a backlight.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: OLED pixels can switch off completely, giving deep blacks, while LCD pixels only block a backlight. Resistive screens respond to pressure that brings two layers into contact, whereas capacitive screens sense the finger's capacitance.

questions.q: The process of converting alternating current into direct current using a p-n junction diode is called
questions.e: A diode conducts in only one direction, so it passes only one half of the AC cycle (half-wave) or both halves flipped (full-wave bridge). Modulation, amplification and oscillation are different electronic functions.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about machine learning:
1. Supervised learning trains a model on labelled data.
2. Reinforcement learning trains a model exclusively on labelled input-output pairs.
3. Clustering of customers into groups without predefined labels is an example of unsupervised learning.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Supervised learning learns from examples with answers, and unsupervised learning finds structure in unlabelled data. Reinforcement learning learns by trial and reward from interacting with an environment.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about large language models (LLMs):
1. They are generally built on the transformer architecture.
2. 'Hallucination' refers to a model producing fluent but false or fabricated output.
3. Because they are trained on very large text datasets, their outputs are guaranteed to be factually accurate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The transformer architecture, introduced in the 2017 paper 'Attention Is All You Need', underlies modern LLMs. They predict likely text, not verified facts, so they can hallucinate.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the IndiaAI Mission:
1. It was approved by the Union Cabinet in 2024.
2. It is implemented by the Ministry of Education.
3. It includes building public compute capacity with GPUs for AI developers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The mission, with an outlay of more than Rs 10,000 crore, was approved in March 2024 and is led by MeitY through the IndiaAI Independent Business Division, aiming at compute, datasets, foundation models and skilling.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the European Union's AI Act:
1. It applies only to AI systems developed by companies headquartered in the EU.
2. It takes a risk-based approach to regulating AI systems.
3. It prohibits certain uses of AI deemed to carry unacceptable risk, such as social scoring by public authorities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Act sorts AI into unacceptable, high, limited and minimal risk, with stricter duties for higher risk. It also applies to providers outside the EU if their systems are placed on the EU market or their output is used there.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about quantum computing:
1. A qubit can exist in a superposition of the states 0 and 1.
2. Quantum entanglement correlates the states of qubits in ways not possible for classical bits.
3. Quantum computers will replace classical computers for all everyday tasks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Superposition and entanglement give quantum computers an advantage for specific problems such as factoring or simulating molecules. They are not expected to replace classical machines for general tasks.

questions.q:
With reference to the National Quantum Mission (NQM) of India, consider the following statements:
1. It is implemented by the Department of Atomic Energy.
2. It was approved by the Union Cabinet in April 2023.
3. It sets up four thematic hubs covering quantum computing, communication, sensing and metrology, and materials and devices.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The NQM runs from 2023-24 to 2030-31 and aims to develop intermediate-scale quantum computers with 50 to 1000 physical qubits. It is implemented by the Department of Science and Technology.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Quantum computers are considered a long-term threat to widely used public-key encryption such as RSA.
Statement-II: Shor's algorithm can factorise large integers efficiently on a sufficiently powerful quantum computer.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: RSA's security rests on the difficulty of factoring the product of two large primes on classical machines. A large quantum computer running Shor's algorithm would break that, which is why post-quantum cryptography standards are being developed.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about cyber security institutions in India:
1. CERT-In functions under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
2. The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) functions under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
3. The National Critical Information Infrastructure Protection Centre (NCIIPC) functions under the National Technical Research Organisation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: CERT-In is the national agency for cyber incident response under the IT Act, and NCIIPC, set up under Section 70A, protects critical information infrastructure. I4C is a body of the Ministry of Home Affairs.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Cyber threat) with List-II (Description):
List-I
A. Phishing
B. Ransomware
C. Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS)
D. Zero-day exploit
List-II
1. Floods a target with traffic from many sources to make it unavailable
2. Uses deceptive messages to trick users into revealing credentials
3. Attacks a software flaw not yet known to the vendor
4. Encrypts a victim's data and demands payment for release
questions.e: Phishing is deception, ransomware is extortion by encryption, DDoS is overload, and a zero-day is an attack with 'zero days' of notice to the vendor.
questions.h: Phish = Fish for your password with bait.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023:
1. A Data Principal is the individual to whom the personal data relates.
2. A Data Fiduciary determines the purpose and means of processing personal data.
3. It applies to personal data in non-digital form even if that data is never digitised.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Act covers digital personal data, including personal data collected offline that is later digitised. It sets up the Data Protection Board of India to adjudicate breaches.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Information Technology Act, 2000:
1. It gives legal recognition to electronic records and digital signatures.
2. It was repealed by the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.
3. Section 66A was struck down by the Supreme Court in Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Section 66A criminalised 'offensive' online messages and was struck down as violating free speech under Article 19(1)(a). The DPDP Act amended some provisions of the IT Act but did not repeal it.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's digital public infrastructure:
1. The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) was developed by the National Payments Corporation of India.
2. The Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) is a government-owned online marketplace that sells goods directly to consumers.
3. Under the Account Aggregator framework, financial data is shared with the user's consent through RBI-regulated entities.
4. DigiLocker is a platform run by the Reserve Bank of India.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: UPI is an NPCI product and Account Aggregators are RBI-regulated consent managers. ONDC is an open network protocol that lets buyers and sellers on different apps transact, not a marketplace, and DigiLocker belongs to MeitY.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Bitcoin is legal tender in India.
2. The digital rupee (e-rupee) is a digital form of legal tender issued by the Reserve Bank of India.
3. The RBI began a pilot of the retail digital rupee in December 2022.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A CBDC is a sovereign digital currency, unlike private cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin, which are not legal tender in India. The wholesale pilot began on 1 November 2022 and the retail pilot on 1 December 2022.
questions.s: RBI press releases, Nov and Dec 2022

questions.q: Which one of the following features makes records on a blockchain difficult to alter?
o: Each block contains the cryptographic hash of the previous block
All records are stored on a single central server
Records are stored only in encrypted form without any link between them
Each transaction is approved by the government
questions.e: Changing one block changes its hash and breaks the link in every later block, and the ledger is copied across many nodes. A single central server would be a single point of failure and is not a blockchain feature.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 5G:
1. India launched 5G services in October 2022.
2. In non-standalone (NSA) mode, 5G radio networks depend on the 4G core network.
3. The massive machine-type communication (mMTC) use case targets ultra-low latency for applications such as remote surgery.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The three 5G usage scenarios are eMBB (high speed), URLLC (ultra-reliable low latency) and mMTC (very large numbers of IoT devices). The remote surgery claim fits URLLC, not mMTC.
questions.h: e = Enhanced speed, U = Ultra-low delay, m = Many things.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Telecommunications Act, 2023 requires spectrum for satellite services to be allocated only through auction.
2. The Bharat 6G Vision document was released in March 2023.
3. The Telecommunications Act, 2023 repeals the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 2023 Act replaces the Telegraph Act of 1885 and the Wireless Telegraphy Act of 1933. It lists satellite services among those with administrative assignment of spectrum, not auction.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Cloud concept) with List-II (Description):
List-I
A. Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
B. Platform as a Service (PaaS)
C. Software as a Service (SaaS)
D. Edge computing
List-II
1. Finished applications delivered over the internet without managing underlying infrastructure
2. Virtualised servers, storage and networking rented on demand
3. A platform for developers to build and deploy applications without managing servers
4. Processing data near where it is generated instead of in a distant data centre
questions.e: IaaS gives the raw computing, PaaS adds a development platform and SaaS delivers the finished application, each step hiding more of the stack from the user. Edge computing shortens response time for IoT and autonomous systems.

questions.q:
Statement-I: IPv6 provides a far larger address space than IPv4.
Statement-II: IPv6 addresses are 64 bits long.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: IPv4 has 32-bit addresses (about 4.3 billion), which are exhausted. IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses, so Statement-II is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about BharatNet:
1. It aims to connect Gram Panchayats with optical fibre.
2. It is overseen by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
3. It has been funded through the Universal Service Obligation Fund, now replaced by the Digital Bharat Nidhi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: BharatNet, earlier the National Optical Fibre Network, is a Department of Telecommunications project to provide broadband to villages. The Telecommunications Act 2023 renamed the USOF as Digital Bharat Nidhi.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Digital platform) with List-II (Purpose):
List-I
A. UMANG
B. e-Sanjeevani
C. GeM
D. DIKSHA
List-II
1. National telemedicine service
2. Public procurement portal
3. Unified mobile app for central and state government services
4. Digital platform for school education
questions.e: UMANG is a one-stop app for government services, e-Sanjeevani offers teleconsultation, GeM (Government e-Marketplace) handles procurement and DIKSHA serves teachers and students.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Supercomputing Mission:
1. It is jointly steered by the Department of Science and Technology and MeitY.
2. It is implemented by C-DAC and the Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru.
3. The supercomputer Pratyush is installed at the National Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasting, Noida.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Pratyush is at the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology, Pune, while the NCMRWF in Noida hosts Mihir. Both are used for weather and climate modelling.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about deepfakes:
1. They are synthetic media created using deep learning techniques.
2. Deepfake techniques cannot be used to clone a person's voice.
3. Generative adversarial networks use a generator and a discriminator that compete with each other.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A GAN's generator produces fakes and its discriminator tries to detect them, so both improve. Deepfake techniques cover face swap and voice cloning, so the claim that voice cannot be cloned is wrong.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Li-Fi cannot be used to connect devices across rooms through opaque walls.
Statement-II: Li-Fi transmits data using visible light.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Li-Fi modulates LED light very rapidly to carry data, and visible light is blocked by opaque walls. Wi-Fi, which uses radio waves, passes through walls, though with weaker signal.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a non-volatile memory, retaining data even when power is switched off?
questions.e: Flash memory, used in SSDs, pen drives and phones, stores charge in floating-gate cells that holds without power. DRAM, SRAM and cache lose their contents when power is lost.

questions.q: Augmented reality (AR) differs from virtual reality (VR) in that AR
o: overlays digital information on the user's view of the real world
creates a fully computer-generated environment replacing the real world
can be used only with a head-mounted display
requires the user to be physically absent from the real surroundings
questions.e: AR adds layers such as navigation arrows or filters to the live camera view, and it can run on a phone. VR shuts out the real world and immerses the user in a simulated one.
